clue.text: Tender love god, also female upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters built so far are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
also means too

explanation.surface: A tender Cupid figure and a woman are both upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EROSTOOF over, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet that are sore after walking feel tender, so the adjective footsore fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Worries over small pet

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: worries as a noun are cares
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a little pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like a noun, an animal, but it is the verb: to stroke fondly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to stroke them affectionately, which is exactly what a caress is as a verb.

clue.text: Free beer laid out around time

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter for time
laid out suggests the letters are spread around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Free beer has been set out on the table for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BEER LAID to LIBERAED, and 'around' puts that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone liberated has been set at liberty, which makes them free, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Treat your old well

parts.note: to treat an illness is to heal it
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned request: treat your well, as in look after your water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well means being in good health, so healthy is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Not really keen to see vagrant

parts.note: no can mean not, as in 'no better'
mad about something means extremely keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone is unenthusiastic about meeting a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders without a fixed home, as a vagrant does, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Manacle with copper principally in bad mood

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the word for a bad mood

parts.note: to be in a huff is to be in a sulk or bad mood
and can mean with, as in 'fish and chips'

indicators.note: principally means only the main, opening letter of copper is taken

explanation.surface: A policeman in a sulk clamps on the cuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ANDC inside HUFF. 'copper' is a British slang word for a police officer, which fits the picture of handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal shackle for the wrist, which is what a handcuff is; both work as verbs too.

clue.text: Beginning to pen line for article

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the cause of something is its beginning or origin

explanation.surface: Someone starts to write a line for a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing, but it means enclose, as a pen holds sheep. 'article' is not a newspaper piece but a section of a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: An article in a contract or treaty is a separate numbered provision, which is a clause.

clue.text: Type of garment, ancient primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: A description of a kind of clothing worn mainly in ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its first letters spell the answer, and it describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the draped outer robe of ancient Roman citizens, a garment of the ancient world.

clue.text: Unpreventable ban or exile abroad

indicators.note: abroad means spread far and wide, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A ban or sending someone abroad into exile that cannot be stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexorable cannot be stopped or halted by any persuasion, so it is unpreventable.

clue.text: Some get here almost spiritual

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arriving here nearly feels like a spiritual experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something delicate and heavenly, not of this world, close in sense to spiritual.

clue.text: Passion is reportedly more exhausting

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a harder task is more exhausting

explanation.surface: Passion is said to be more tiring than people think.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound works with a dropped H and a non-rhotic British accent, where HARDER is said 'arder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or burning feeling, a direct synonym for passion.

clue.text: Has to hurt trapping old walrus?

indicators.note: trapping means the outer pieces catch and hold another inside them

parts.note: must means has to
to hurt is to ache

explanation.surface: Something must be hurt so that an old walrus can be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walrus' looks like the animal, but it is an example of the answer: a walrus is a thick drooping style, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus is a thick moustache that droops over the mouth like the animal's whiskers; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Desist about English being reserved

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to desist is to quit doing something

explanation.surface: A shy English person is told to stop going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is undemonstrative and says little, which is to be quiet.

clue.text: In woods, thanks sweetheart providing anticipation

indicators.note: In means the word for thanks goes inside the word for woods

parts.note: a forest is a large area of woods
ta is British informal for thanks
the heart of sweet, its central letter, is E

explanation.surface: Thanking a lover in the woods gives a hint of what is to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it is the heart of 'sweet', the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is a small early sample of something to come, so it gives anticipation of it.

clue.text: Bachelors in action getting sordid

indicators.note: in places the bachelors inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so the plural is BAs

explanation.surface: Single men caught up in something that turns grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bachelors' looks like single men, but it is the degree BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Debased means lowered in moral quality, degraded, which is close to sordid.

clue.text: One acted out amusing story

indicators.note: acted out suggests the letters are played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone performed a funny tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short entertaining account of a real incident, which is an amusing story.

clue.text: Reveal criminal's carrying iron shackles initially

indicators.note: carrying means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: con is a convict, so criminal's, criminal is, gives CON + S
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of shackles is used

explanation.surface: A convict wearing iron shackles reveals all.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'criminal's' stands for 'is', so the S is part of the container that 'carrying' signals; 'iron' and 'shackles' suit the convict picture but only supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to admit a secret or wrongdoing, which is to reveal it.

clue.text: Furtive about cooker left dirty

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: sly means secretive and furtive
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone sneaky has left the cooker filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenly means untidy and careless about cleanliness, so close to dirty.

clue.text: Some autopsy chests to find souls

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pathologists open up chests at a post-mortem looking for the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or spirit, so psyches are souls.

clue.text: Infant beginning to love making commotion

parts.note: a babe is a baby or infant

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of love is taken

explanation.surface: A baby starts to love making a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A babel is a confused noise of many voices, after the biblical tower, so a commotion.

clue.text: Broadcast from excellent band

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, and the 1 is read as the letter I
a ring is a band, as on a finger

explanation.surface: A transmission from a first-rate group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like musicians, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An airing of a programme is a showing of it on radio or television, which is a broadcast.

clue.text: Slur like individual imbibing martini finally

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a person is an individual

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of martini is taken

explanation.surface: Insulting someone, as if they were downing a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging remark about someone's character, which is a slur.

clue.text: Article supports fake healer

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: a sham is a fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs a quack doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal priest believed to cure the sick through spirits, a traditional healer.

clue.text: Ring of King Charles II's mistress

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A ring given to the mistress of King Charles II.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery, but it is the sound of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the sound of a bell tolled slowly, especially for a death, so a ring.

clue.text: Writer could be boring study

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: An author's work might be a dull piece of study.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet and dramatist, a famous writer.

clue.text: He's a card, performing parlour game

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a show, being acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A comic is acting in a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a playing card, but it is a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a guessing game where words are mimed, played at home parties, so a parlour game.

clue.text: Tick includes oddly lumped part payment

indicators.note: includes means one piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: a tick is a moment or instant

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and fifth letters of lumped are taken

explanation.surface: A credit purchase includes a payment, oddly lumped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is British slang for credit, which suits the surface, but it is a moment: INSTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one of several portions in which a debt is paid, so a part payment.

clue.text: Friend may be completely unknown

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all alone'
Y is a mathematical unknown, as in algebra

explanation.surface: A friend might be a total stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side who supports you, close in sense to friend.
